stated: Plant at least 60 million trees a year, helping to restore woodland habitats, increase the use of sustainable wood in construction, and reach net zero.

source.quote: Plant at least 60 million trees a year, helping to restore woodland habitats, increase the use of sustainable wood in construction, and reach net zero.

bearing_set.reason: Planting 60 million trees a year directly addresses emissions trajectories (carbon sequestration toward net zero) and habitat/nature restoration, earning a real verdict on clean environment.

The stated aim of increasing sustainable wood in construction creates a long-term domestic timber-industry and supply-chain effect (productivity, business formation, construction-sector opportunity), diverging significantly across near and long horizons as trees mature over decades.

Planting at this scale requires substantial ongoing public expenditure (grants, land incentives, management); at plausible per-tree delivery costs the annual commitment runs to hundreds of millions, materially affecting the funded-vs-borrowed balance and the debt path.

membership_note: O6 is the primary bearing. O13 earns a dual-horizon verdict via the timber/construction mechanism explicitly stated. O12 earns a verdict because the fiscal cost of tripling-plus current planting rates is concrete and non-trivial. O1 (housing affordability via timber-frame) was considered but the causal chain is too attenuated and long-term to clear the non-negligible bar independently.
